title: Descent of the clopen scalar comparison
statement: Let X be a scheme and j_i:Y_i→X a finite pairwise disjoint clopen cover. Use the actual small pro-etale module sheaves, scalar extension presentations p_a and their normalized successive compositor n, exact restrictions r_i and r_D,i, canonical cochain computation morphisms c_a(P), normalized identity units, and scalar comparison interfaces of [def-pur-clopen-derived-scalar-comparison-data]. For any fixed global presentations p with normalization n, and component presentations q_i with normalizations m_i, there exists a comparison family d_i. Its ordinary isomorphism E_a⋙r_i ≅ r_i⋙E_(a_i) sends s⊗x to s⊗x. Its chain comparison has degree k equal to that ordinary comparison on P^k. Its derived comparison L E_a⋙r_D,i ≅ r_D,i⋙L E_(a_i) satisfies the exact canonical computation square representative on every flat-term K-flat P. Any derived natural transformation satisfying that same representative square on all such P equals its forward map. These are the sections, degree, representative and unique predicates; computed, extended, units and compositor coherence are not asserted here.

proof.text: Use the proved ordinary scalar restriction comparison, including its pure tensor formula. Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex degreewise; its component in degree k is definitionally the ordinary comparison on P.X k.

Every cochain complex admits a quasi-isomorphism from a K-flat complex with tensor-flat terms. Convert the tensor-flatness clause to IsFlatOnSite through siteSheafTensorRightIso. The homotopy quotient is full and surjective on objects. The resolving full homotopy subcategory therefore localizes to the entire derived category, and restriction of natural transformations along its cochain representatives is fully faithful. This is the one-variable specialization of the proved resolving-representative whiskering argument, using its restriction_localization and fullyFaithfulWhiskeringOfFullEssSurj helpers.

Package the canonical computation morphisms as a natural transformation from Q followed by derived extension to termwise ordinary extension followed by Q. Normalization.computed makes this transformation invertible on flat-term K-flat complexes. Clopen tensor/K-flat detection makes it invertible also after component restriction. The exact restriction localization factors and the chain comparison give two invertible maps from the restricted derived functors to the same chainwise functor. Their quotient descends uniquely by the preceding fully faithful restriction. The preimage is an isomorphism and satisfies precisely the representative square. For any competing natural transformation, that square and cancellation of the same invertible computation map identify its restriction with this preimage; faithfulness gives uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem clopen_scalar_comparison_descent
    (X : Scheme.{t}) (I : Type w) [Finite I] (Y : I → Scheme.{t})
    (j : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ X) [∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (j i)] [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (j i)]
    (hd : Pairwise (fun i k ↦ Disjoint (Set.range (j i)) (Set.range (j k))))
    (hc : ∀ x : X, ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (j i))
    (p : Presentations.{t, u} X)
    (n : Normalization.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max (u + 1) (t + 2)}
      (C := X.ProEt) (J := topology X) (hD := derived.{t, u} X) @p)
    (q : ∀ i, Presentations.{t, u} (Y i))
    (m : ∀ i, Normalization.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max (u + 1) (t + 2)}
      (C := (Y i).ProEt) (J := topology (Y i)) (hD := derived.{t, u} (Y i))
      (fun {R S} a ↦ q i (R := R) (S := S) a))
    : ∃ d : ∀ i, Comparison.{t, u} (j i) @p
        (fun {R S} a ↦ q i (R := R) (S := S) a),
      ∀ i, (d i).sections ∧ (d i).degree ∧ (d i).representative ∧ (d i).unique
